body: Our paper, [Real-time lane-level abnormal traffic detection on freeways using sparse telematics data](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aap.2026.108607), is published in *Accident Analysis & Prevention*.
title: Sparse telematics for lane-level abnormal traffic detection

body: Awarded the **Roger Wilmot Memorial Fund Travel Grant**, administered by UW E-RIDE, to support planned participation in **TRB 2027**, with a focus on multimodal AI, vehicle telematics, and research partnerships for rural transportation safety. [Details](/lab/#funding-and-awards).
title: Roger Wilmot travel grant for TRB 2027

body: The **Wisconsin Highway Delay Causation Study (2025–2026)**, supported by WisDOT, is complete. The study examines recurring and nonrecurring highway delay and contributing factors across Wisconsin. [Final report](https://wisconsindot.gov/documents2/research/0092-25-22-final-report.pdf).
title: Wisconsin highway delay study completed

body: I was selected as a **2026–2027 UW Data Science Faculty Fellow** to develop vehicle-telematics methods for real-time roadway monitoring and proactive safety management on Wyoming highways, supported by the UW Data Science Center. [Details](/lab/#funding-and-awards).
title: UW Data Science Faculty Fellowship

body: Awarded a **Wyoming NASA EPSCoR Faculty Research Award** to develop lightweight vision-language models for interpreting roadway weather from camera imagery, with natural-language explanations and evaluation on edge devices. [Details](/lab/#funding-and-awards).
title: NASA EPSCoR award for roadway weather AI

body: **SCOUT-WY** received support through the UW CEPS Engineering Initiative seed grant program for 2026–2027 to link vehicle observations across sparse roadside cameras and support travel-time estimation, traffic monitoring, and anomaly detection on rural Wyoming corridors. [Details](/lab/#funding-and-awards).
title: SCOUT-WY receives seed funding

body: New preprint: [Behavior-Grounded Lane Representation Learning for Multi-Task Traffic Digital Twins](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01901), introducing GeoLaneRep for behavior-aware traffic digital twins.
title: GeoLaneRep preprint

body: We will present our work, [CrashSight](https://drivex-workshop.github.io/cvpr2026/static/pdf/27_CrashSight_A_Phase_Aware_In.pdf), at the DriveX Workshop at CVPR 2026.
title: CrashSight at the CVPR DriveX Workshop

body: Our proposed **Wyoming Center for Artificial Intelligence in Transportation (WyCAIT)** received support from the UW Science Institute for 2026–2027 to advance multimodal sensing, resilient AI, and corridor digital twins for rural transportation safety, operations, and workforce development. [Details](/lab/#funding-and-awards).
title: Support for the proposed WyCAIT center

body: New preprint: [An Agentic Workflow for Detecting Personally Identifiable Information in Crash Narratives](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15369), presenting a locally deployable workflow for privacy-sensitive crash data processing.
title: Agentic privacy workflow preprint

body: New preprint: [V2X-QA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02710), a dataset and benchmark for multimodal large language models in autonomous driving across ego, infrastructure, and cooperative views.
title: V2X-QA preprint
